messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cont-batch worker error rate spike in us-east-1 (svc: runtime-proxy). KV cache eviction rate increased 12x, paging observed. root cause suspected: sudden max_batch_tokens growth due to malformed traffic. Pagerduty: paging oncall.
Alex R: Acked. I'm pulling logs + perf graphs.
Maya K: I'm on infra, looking at node-level OOM and disk IOPS — I see heavy page-in activity on 3 hosts in pool-gpu-a. Paging is saturating NVMe.
Jun T: Runtime team here. Can you paste the request pattern? any long sequences?
Alex R: Paste of a sampled tail of requests: 
```
{ "seq_len": 4096, "prompt": "<<very long chat>>", "policy": "continuous-batching" }
{ "seq_len": 1536 }
{ "seq_len": 4096 }
```
Most heavy ones are 4k sequences.
Maya K: That explains it — cont-batch max_batch_tokens (global) is currently 65536, but max_num_seqs was liberal. Combined with high seq_len, some batches ballooned to ~90k tokens and blew the KV memory working set, leading to eviction and paging.
Elaine S: Support: observed customer reports of 10-30s latency; a few 504s. Major customers hitting generation endpoints. They're asking if this is a config bug or attack.
Jun T: Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) reduce CONT_BATCH_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS to 16384 (global) 2) set CONT_BATCH_MAX_NUM_SEQS to 8 3) bump per-request timeout to avoid long tail retries 4) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant (cpu-quant) for new requests. Which can we do fast?
Maya K: I can push the global flags to the control plane for us-east; it'll take ~90s to roll to proxies.
Alex R: I will craft a safe flag rollout. Can we also disable continuous batching for the problematic model id (gptx-4o-large) as an emergency kill switch? That stops batch-induced KV pressure.
Jun T: Yes, we have a flag: model.cont_batch_enabled=false per model. I can flip for that model now.
Maya K: Doing the config change now: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/flags
{ "scope": "us-east-1","CONT_BATCH_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS": 16384 }
```
Rolling to proxy pool.
deploy-bot: Deploy started for flag change (rollout id: fr-2891).
Alex R: Changing model flag next: setting gptx-4o-large.cont_batch_enabled=false in us-east.
Jun T: Applied. Confirming runtime no longer accepts cont-batch for that model.
Maya K: I see NVMe pageins drop 80% and eviction rate trending down. Good sign.
Elaine S: Customer impact update: latency from 10-30s -> now 2-6s for most requests. One customer still seeing higher latency — looks like they're pinned to a dedidcated pool that hasn't received the flag yet. Opening a targeted roll for that pool.
Alex R: For the dedicated pool I'll directly update instance config and restart proxies one-by-one to avoid cold cache storms. Doing now.
Oncall Pager: note: PD escalation not required, keeping oncall informed.
Jun T: Root cause hypothesis for post-incident writeup: permissive defaults for CONT_BATCH_MAX_NUM_SEQS combined with unbounded client sequence lengths allowed occasional massive batches. The autoscaling and eviction thresholds didn't prevent working set blowup, so disk paging destroyed latency SLOs.
Priya D: Quick question — did any of our autoscalers trigger node scale-ups?
Maya K: Yes, autoscaler kicked in but scaling lagged behind the immediate KV pressure and created more churn. We'll add a guard to suspend aggressive scale-down when eviction_rate > threshold.
Alex R: Action items (short term):
- [ ] Roll back cont-batch for gptx-4o-large globally until we have safe limits.
- [ ] Set global CONT_BATCH_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=16384 and CONT_BATCH_MAX_NUM_SEQS=8.
- [ ] Increase default request timeout for generation endpoints by 2x to avoid retry storms.
- [ ] Notify impacted customers (Elaine to lead).
Jun T: Action items (longer):
- [ ] Add per-model batch ceiling enforcement in runtime.
- [ ] Circuit-breaker: if KV eviction rate > X for Y seconds, fallback to non-cont-batch path.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboard: per-model max_batch_tokens distribution + seq_len histograms.
Maya K: I'm updating the runbook with mitigation steps and the exact commands used.
Alex R: Elaine, can you ping cust success with a short blurb? "We experienced elevated latencies due to large batched requests triggering cache evictions; mitigation applied, working on root cause and permanent guardrails."
Elaine S: Sent note to affected customers and posted status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2891234567 (internal link).
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Flag rollout fr-2891 completed. Model flag change completed.
Jun T: Monitoring — latency and error rate trending back to baseline. We'll keep the incident channel open for 3 hours for any regressions.
Alex R: Recording timeline and tagging for postmortem. Please add any logs or queries you used.
Priya D: For the postmortem: we should consider defaulting CONT_BATCH_MAX_NUM_SEQS to 4 and adding a hard token cap per-batch in the scheduler.
Maya K: Noted. I'll create an infra PR for eviction threshold guards and scaling policy tweak.
Elaine S: Closing loop with customers now.
Alex R: Thanks team. Moving to incident review — will schedule a 40m follow-up in #postmortems later today.
